phenomena.claim: Progressive, time-resolved decoherence of a mesoscopic superposition ('meter') observed in cavity QED, with decoherence rate growing with separation of the superposed states
phenomena.source: Brune, Hagley, Dreyer, Maitre, Maali, Wunderlich, Raimond & Haroche, Phys. Rev. Lett. 77, 4887-4890 (1996) — title/author/venue/year verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: single platform entry; rate-vs-separation detail is body-level, cited at title/abstract level here

phenomena.claim: Environment-controlled decoherence of matter waves observed with tunable rates: collisional (background gas pressure) and thermal-emission (internal temperature) channels
phenomena.source: Hornberger, Uttenthaler, Brezger, Hackermueller, Arndt & Zeilinger, Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 160401 (2003); Hackermueller, Hornberger, Brezger, Zeilinger & Arndt, Nature 427, 711-714 (2004) — both verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: quantitative agreement with decoherence theory asserted at title level; coefficient-level agreement is body content for Stage 2

phenomena.claim: Macroscopic superpositions are not observed to persist
phenomena.caveat: stated as a not-observed; collapse-model parameter space only partially constrained (see quantum_mechanics record domain_of_validity)

formalism.claim: Reduced dynamics of a subsystem (uncorrelated initial state) is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) map with an operator-sum representation; every CPTP map dilates to unitary evolution plus partial trace (Stinespring/Choi)
formalism.source: Stinespring, Proc. Am. Math. Soc. 6, 211-216 (1955); Choi, Linear Algebra Appl. 10, 285-290 (1975) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: complete positivity of the reduced map presumes an uncorrelated initial system-environment state (see domain_of_validity)

formalism.claim: The generator of a completely positive quantum dynamical semigroup has the GKLS (Lindblad) form
formalism.source: Lindblad, Commun. Math. Phys. 48, 119-130 (1976); Gorini, Kossakowski & Sudarshan, J. Math. Phys. 17, 821-825 (1976) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: Markovian/semigroup assumption; GKS proof is finite-dimensional, Lindblad's covers bounded generators

formalism.claim: The Nakajima-Zwanzig projection-operator technique gives an exact master equation for the reduced state with a memory (convolution) kernel
formalism.source: Nakajima, Prog. Theor. Phys. 20, 948-959 (1958); Zwanzig, J. Chem. Phys. 33, 1338-1341 (1960) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: exact but the kernel is generally not computable without approximation; original papers are transport/ensemble-method formulations, standard open-systems form is textbook-consolidated

formalism.claim: The influence functional captures the environment's entire effect on the reduced system path integral (Feynman-Vernon); for linear dissipative environments it is Gaussian and yields the quantum Brownian motion master equation (Caldeira-Leggett)
formalism.source: Feynman & Vernon, Ann. Phys. 24, 118-173 (1963); Caldeira & Leggett, Physica A 121, 587-616 (1983) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: closed forms for Gaussian/linear environments; the high-temperature Caldeira-Leggett equation is not CP at all times

primitives.claim: The system-environment tensor split and the interaction Hamiltonian are declared inputs of every open-system construction, not derived objects
primitives.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_CHECK_05_CASE_02_DECOHERENCE.md input ledger ('H = H_S + H_E + H_int -> ASSUMED (declared construction)'); cf. quantum_mechanics record primitives (factorization not intrinsic, Cotler-Penington-Ranard)
primitives.caveat: the preferred-factorization question is recorded in the quantum_mechanics domain record

derived_objects.claim: Decoherence (suppression of interference in reduced states) is derived within closed unitary QM plus coarse-graining: closed unitary dynamics with orthogonal environmental records produce reduced-state decoherence while preserving a pure global entangled state
derived_objects.caveat: in-house, unreviewed; scope: the repaired Experiment P model class (minimal closed system-apparatus-environment with exact finite-dimensional unitaries); 'universal beyond tested model class' is recorded OUTSIDE_SCOPE

derived_objects.claim: Community decoherence theory is DERIVED + EFFECTIVE: decoherence is a theorem of the declared unitary system-environment model (partial trace of unitary evolution), with off-diagonal decay in the pointer basis
derived_objects.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_CHECK_05_CASE_02_DECOHERENCE.md final classification; primary sources Joos & Zeh, Z. Phys. B 59, 223-243 (1985); Zurek, Rev. Mod. Phys. 75, 715-775 (2003) — both verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: construction choice (pointer coupling) is declared, not derived

derived_objects.claim: The pointer basis is selected by the form of the system-environment interaction (environment-induced superselection)
derived_objects.source: Zurek, Phys. Rev. D 24, 1516-1525 (1981); Zurek, Rev. Mod. Phys. 75, 715-775 (2003) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: basis is derived GIVEN the declared interaction; the interaction itself is an input (see primitives)

derived_objects.claim: A closed quantum substrate plus coarse-graining reproduces the full effective open-system phenomenology: decoherence, memory kernels, dissipation, noise, apparent openness
derived_objects.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_PICTURE_01.md LEVEL 4 item 1 ('[T for the mechanism; H as ontology]... standard physics, not GRUT property'); Stage 2: the archive is in-house and cannot verify a COMMUNITY-DERIVED entry — cite a community source at construction level (e.g. Breuer & Petruccione, The Theory of Open Quantum Systems, Oxford UP 2002) or narrow the claim to the linear-environment case already carried by the verified Feynman-Vernon and Caldeira-Leggett entries
derived_objects.caveat: [T] for the mechanism only; as ontology it is hypothesis-grade [H]; 'full phenomenology' is the archive's classification, broader than any single checked citation

empirical_inputs.claim: Bath structure — spectral density, temperature, coupling constants — enters open-system models as declared/fitted input, not as derived content
empirical_inputs.source: Caldeira & Leggett, Physica A 121, 587-616 (1983) as the canonical parametrized-bath construction — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
empirical_inputs.caveat: the spectral-density-as-input reading is standard-textbook; cited at construction level

empirical_inputs.claim: Branch weights (diagonal populations after decoherence) enter as initial-state data — inherited, not dynamically derived
empirical_inputs.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_CHECK_04_EXPERIMENT_P_ADJUDICATION.md §9 item 8 and §10 ('Branch weights are inherited from the initial amplitudes and are not dynamically derived within this model class'); concordant community ledger: RC-05 C2 'Born weights of initial amplitudes -> INHERITED_STATE_DATA'
empirical_inputs.caveat: within the tested model class; not a universal disproof of Born-rule derivability

constants.claim: No new fundamental constant enters open-system/decoherence theory: decoherence and relaxation rates are derived functions of hbar, declared couplings, and bath parameters
constants.source: absence recorded against this record's verified formalism entries (GKLS, Nakajima-Zwanzig, influence functional introduce no constant beyond hbar and model inputs); archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 Q17 minimum input set lists no open-systems constant
constants.caveat: collapse-model parameters (e.g. CSL rate) are constants of ALTERNATIVE theories, out of scope here

symmetries.claim: CPTP maps are contractive for the trace distance (data-processing inequality); the semigroup composition law is the structural invariance of the Markovian theory
symmetries.source: Stage 2: cite Ruskai, Rev. Math. Phys. 6, 1147 (1994) (trace-norm contractivity under stochastic maps) or equivalent standard source at abstract level
symmetries.caveat: contractivity is the basis of trace-distance non-Markovianity witnesses (see open_problems)

limits.claim: GKLS/Lindblad dynamics is recovered from underlying Hamiltonian system-plus-reservoir models in the weak-coupling (Davies) limit
limits.source: Davies, Commun. Math. Phys. 39, 91-110 (1974), 'Markovian master equations' — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
limits.caveat: rigorous derivations require weak-coupling/secular assumptions; strong coupling and structured baths fall outside (see domain_of_validity)

limits.claim: Classical mechanics is recovered as a limit of QM via decoherence + hbar->0
limits.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_PICTURE_01.md LEVEL 3 'QM ──LIMIT_OF──▶ classical mechanics [T] CLOSED (decoherence + hbar->0)'
limits.caveat: edge type LIMIT_RELATION; duplicate of the quantum_mechanics record entry, carried here because decoherence is the mechanism

known_connections.caveat: closed at the reduced-dynamics layer; outcome layer explicitly excluded (see known_disconnects)

known_connections.claim: Boundary entry (gravity-side absorptive response): the one-loop graviton self-energy on de Sitter space carries a fully certified absorptive response through H^6 that is not representable by the tested class of stationary amplitude/frequency dressings — every certified term is non-analytic in omega, so no local counterterm or contact field redefinition can generate or remove the certified content — with stationarity and memory anti-correlated in the certified response — a standard-QFT in-house computation connecting open-system response/memory structure to gravity
known_connections.source: archive: origin/physics-final:GRUT_FINAL_SYNTHESIS_01.md §0 stopping statement and §1a-1c (T3 chain custody: K2 partition closure through T3-09B; amended per T3-08A AMENDMENT_01)

known_disconnects.claim: Decoherence does NOT yield a definite outcome
known_disconnects.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_PICTURE_01.md LEVEL 3 'decoherence ──✗──▶ definite outcome [E] OPEN (P + RC-05 C2, cross-validated)'; RC-04 §10 'Definite outcome is therefore not derived by the tested unitary/coarse-graining route'
known_disconnects.caveat: tested route: closed unitary + coarse-graining; community concurrence recorded (Zurek RMP 2003: outcome problem explicitly NOT solved by decoherence alone, per RC-05 C2 source ledger)

known_disconnects.claim: Decoherence observables alone do not determine branch weights
known_disconnects.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_CHECK_04_EXPERIMENT_P_ADJUDICATION.md §9 item 8 Control H NARROWED — 'Permitted claim only: decoherence observables alone do not determine branch weights'
known_disconnects.caveat: the stronger full-reduced-state claim is explicitly prohibited (p0 is itself a reduced-state observable); cross term = 0 for alpha in {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}

known_disconnects.claim: Openness does NOT escape response-reducibility: the RRT-0 no-go rests on LINEARITY — unitary, non-unitary-invertible, non-invertible, CPTP, and Lindblad dynamics are all response-reducible (Delta_n = T^n((E-I)[rho]) uses only linearity); only nonlinear dynamics, nonlinear perturbation, or nonlinear readout can escape
known_disconnects.source: archive: commit 510c105 on origin/rrt0-phase2 ('RRT-1 reducibility correction: the RRT-0 no-go rests on LINEARITY, not invertibility -- a linear-universe-wide response no-go'); numerical confirmation d=4, machine-zero residuals (<= 9.5e-17) on depolarizing, amplitude-damping, rank-collapse, and Lindblad maps
known_disconnects.caveat: in-house, unreviewed; scoped to P1 response-reducibility — P2 state-recoverability needs invertibility, P3 asymptotic-structure and P4 operator-algebra reducibility remain open questions of the supplied dynamics

open_problems.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_PICTURE_01.md LEVEL 0 not-directly-observed list + LEVEL 6 rank 1 ('every known route adds structure... None derives it from closed dynamics')
open_problems.caveat: shared with the quantum_mechanics record; decoherence-specific face: the derivation chain stops at the reduced-state layer

open_problems.claim: Definition, classification, and quantification of quantum non-Markovianity remain an active area with several coexisting criteria; no single canonical measure is established
open_problems.source: Breuer, Laine, Piilo & Vacchini, Colloquium: Non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, Rev. Mod. Phys. 88, 021002 (2016) — Crossref + arXiv:1505.01385 abstract verified 2026-09-23 (definition/classification/quantification of memory effects named as the review's subject)
open_problems.caveat: inequivalence of specific named measures is body-level content, not re-derived here; trace-distance (BLP) witnesses have been measured in photonic setups — Stage 2: cite Liu et al., Nat. Phys. 7, 931 (2011) if load-bearing

observables.claim: Decoherence rates via interference-visibility decay and conditional field signals, measured as functions of controlled environment parameters (photon-number separation, gas pressure, internal temperature)
observables.source: Brune et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 77, 4887 (1996); Hornberger et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 160401 (2003); Hackermueller et al., Nature 427, 711 (2004) — all verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
observables.caveat: agreement-with-theory strength is body-level; entry records the observable class

alternative_formulations.claim: Stochastic unravelings (Monte Carlo wave function / quantum trajectories) are equivalent to the Lindblad master equation at the ensemble-average level
alternative_formulations.source: Dalibard, Castin & Molmer, Phys. Rev. Lett. 68, 580-583 (1992) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
alternative_formulations.caveat: unraveling is not unique; individual trajectories carry no extra ontological weight in the standard reading

alternative_formulations.claim: Path-integral (influence functional) and operator (master equation) formulations coexist and agree where both apply
alternative_formulations.source: Feynman & Vernon, Ann. Phys. 24, 118 (1963); Caldeira & Leggett, Physica A 121, 587 (1983) (master equation derived from the influence functional) — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
alternative_formulations.caveat: equivalence exercised on linear/Gaussian environments; general statement is textbook-consolidated

domain_of_validity.claim: Complete positivity of reduced dynamics is guaranteed for initially uncorrelated system-environment states; with initial correlations the reduced dynamics need not be completely positive
domain_of_validity.source: Pechukas, Phys. Rev. Lett. 73, 1060-1062 (1994), 'Reduced Dynamics Need Not Be Completely Positive' — verified via Crossref 2026-09-23
domain_of_validity.caveat: subsequent assignment-map literature qualifies the scope; recorded at the original-result level

domain_of_validity.claim: The Lindblad/GKLS description is valid under weak-coupling, Born-Markov, and secular approximations; strong coupling and structured baths require Nakajima-Zwanzig or other non-Markovian tools
domain_of_validity.source: Davies, Commun. Math. Phys. 39, 91-110 (1974) (rigorous weak-coupling limit); Breuer, Laine, Piilo & Vacchini, Rev. Mod. Phys. 88, 021002 (2016) (non-Markovian regime review) — verified via Crossref/arXiv 2026-09-23
domain_of_validity.caveat: boundary stated qualitatively; quantitative breakdown criteria are model-dependent
